## What a dealt pose may say
A position and a turn — never `z` and never a scale, and the TYPE has no room for either.
Siblings keep tree order at equal height, so the card dealt last already shows on top;
thickness is an `at` offset, and lifting the whole pile is its container's `z`, applied once.
A preset that lifted every card would raise a lifted hand twice — the same law layouts obey,
docs.presetsPoses.fan: A hand fan pivoting about a wrist below the picture. The middle card rests exactly where a
single card would — drop a fan into a scene and nothing else moves — and the ends swing down
`spread` is the whole arc, first card to last: more cards pack the same arc tighter. One card
is no fan and comes back unposed.
docs.presetsPoses.stack: A resting stack: each card a whisker past the one under it. Thickness is position, not `z` —
the card dealt last shows on top because tree order says so, and nothing here is lifted.
That is the lesson `Atoms/Transformable` states in prose, dealt: lift the whole pile by its
container's `z` and every card rises exactly once.
docs.presetsPoses.cascade: The same march as a stack, spaced to be read: each card steps far enough that the one under
it still shows its top. A solitaire column is this straight down; turn the step sideways and
the column becomes a dealt river — one call either way.
